seoTitle: How to Build Sub Zaps in Zapier (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Create modular parent and child Zaps in Zapier using Sub Zaps to reuse the same logic across multiple automated workflows.
intro: Once your automations get complex, duplicating the same steps across multiple Zaps becomes hard to maintain. This guide covers Sub Zaps, Zapier's way of splitting a large workflow into a reusable child Zap that any number of parent Zaps can call, so shared logic lives in one place.

steps.heading: Understand parent and child Zaps
steps.body: Learn the concept of Sub Zaps and when modular logic makes sense over a single massive multi-step Zap.

steps.heading: Create the Child Zap
steps.body: Set up a Child Zap using the "Start a Sub Zap" trigger step to define incoming arguments.

steps.heading: Define input fields and test arguments
steps.body: Set custom input fields and test arguments inside the Child Zap to simulate real data.

steps.heading: Build the middle steps and return data
steps.body: Add your functional middle steps, then finish with a "Return From a Sub Zap" action to pass clean data back.

steps.heading: Create the Parent Zap
steps.body: Build a Parent Zap and locate the "Call a Sub Zap" action step to trigger your modular Child Zap.

steps.heading: Map data and test end-to-end
steps.body: Map main data tokens into your Sub Zap inputs, run an end-to-end test, and review error handling for shared assets.

faq.question: What's the difference between a Parent Zap and a Child Zap?
faq.answer: A Parent Zap calls a Sub Zap using the "Call a Sub Zap" action, while the Child Zap contains the reusable logic and starts with the "Start a Sub Zap" trigger.

faq.question: Why would I use Sub Zaps instead of one long Zap?
faq.answer: Sub Zaps let you avoid duplicating the same steps across multiple Zaps, organizing complex logic into reusable modular blocks.

faq.question: How does data get passed back to the main workflow?
faq.answer: The "Return From a Sub Zap" action step passes clean data back from the Child Zap to whichever Parent Zap called it.

faq.question: Who typically needs Sub Zaps?
faq.answer: They're aimed at workflow automation specialists, developers, and advanced operations managers building enterprise-grade logic.
